_comment: Keyed by exact PlantVillage label string from the model's id2label. 'demo' classes have full curated treatment text (Stage 1 validation focus per BUILD-PLAN.md). Any other class the 38-way model predicts falls back to the '_default' entry below so the app never crashes on an out-of-scope class.

_default.description: This result is outside the app's curated disease set. Confidence and treatment guidance may be less reliable.
treatment: Isolate the affected plant if possible to limit spread.
Consult a local agricultural extension office for a confirmed diagnosis.
Retake the photo in good light, focused on a single affected leaf, for a clearer result.

Potato___healthy.description: No signs of disease detected on this potato leaf.
treatment: No treatment needed.
Keep monitoring weekly, especially after rain.

Potato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease (Alternaria solani) causing dark concentric-ring spots on lower leaves, spreading upward.
treatment: Remove and destroy infected leaves.
Apply a chlorothalonil or copper-based fungicide, repeating every 7-10 days.
Rotate crops; avoid planting potatoes/tomatoes in the same soil next season.
Improve airflow between plants and avoid overhead watering.

Potato___Late_blight.description: Aggressive water-mold disease (Phytophthora infestans) — the same pathogen behind the Irish potato famine. Spreads fast in cool, wet weather.
treatment: Act immediately: remove and destroy all infected plant material, do not compost.
Apply a systemic fungicide (e.g. metalaxyl or mancozeb-based) as soon as possible.
Avoid overhead irrigation; water at the base only.
If severe, destroy the whole plant to protect neighboring crops.

Tomato___healthy.description: No signs of disease detected on this tomato leaf.
treatment: No treatment needed.
Keep monitoring weekly, especially in humid conditions.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: Bacterial infection (Xanthomonas spp.) causing small dark water-soaked spots on leaves and fruit.
treatment: Remove infected leaves and destroy them, do not compost.
Apply a copper-based bactericide weekly during wet weather.
Avoid working with wet plants — bacteria spread easily on damp hands and tools.
Use disease-free seed and resistant varieties next season.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: Fungal disease (Alternaria solani) causing dark target-like spots starting on older, lower leaves.
treatment: Remove and destroy affected lower leaves.
Apply a chlorothalonil or copper-based fungicide every 7-10 days.
Mulch around the base to prevent soil splash onto leaves.
Stake or cage plants to improve airflow.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: Fast-spreading water-mold disease (Phytophthora infestans) causing large greasy, dark blotches on leaves and fruit.
treatment: Act immediately: remove and destroy infected material, do not compost.
Apply a systemic fungicide (e.g. chlorothalonil or copper-based) right away.
Avoid overhead watering; water at the base only.
In severe cases, remove the whole plant to protect the rest of the crop.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: No signs of disease detected on this corn leaf.
treatment: No treatment needed.
Keep monitoring weekly, especially during humid growing periods.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: Fungal disease (Puccinia sorghi) causing reddish-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
treatment: Apply a foliar fungicide (e.g. azoxystrobin or propiconazole) if infection is heavy before tasseling.
Plant rust-resistant corn hybrids in future seasons.
Remove volunteer corn plants that can carry the fungus between seasons.
Monitor closely — mild infections often don't need treatment.
